content:
Hi! Here is a PSA that is not Lean-specific but will affect everyone here. Two very big security issues have just been made public, one for TLS encryption certificates and one for PHP. You should install updates right now, on any device that connects to the internet.

  1. PHP has released a patch to fix two security flaws. Attackers can use these flaws to take control of a website if it hasn’t been fixed. If you run a website with PHP (including Wordpress), please make sure to update the PHP version on the server yourself, or reach out to your hosting provider for updates. More info at PHP.net.
    I have taken some of my own websites offline until I have time to install the patch.

  2. Security researchers discovered that some intermediate certificates had easily-guessable secret keys. These certificates are used by protocols like HTTPS, to ensure that no one can intercept your secure internet communications and pretend to be a service you trust. Every device connected to the internet is potentially vulnerable to interception, so make sure you update everything. You might also need to recompile the software you wrote, if it includes CA certificates. More info on the security researchers' website.
    I have verified that all of my personal computers, phones and servers now distrust the certificate authority with the vulnerable keys.

To the best of my knowledge, Lean is not directly affected by these vulnerabilities. But everyone on this Zulip chat uses HTTPS, so would be affected by the certificate vulnerability. Please make sure you are safe.

A note for Lean tooling on the certificate issue: elan, lake, lake exe cache get and git all use your system curl and its CA store. So these tools are vulnerable until the local CA store distrusts the affected roots.

To check, run both commands (on Windows, type curl.exe):

curl https://dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/
curl https://dv-g3b-aaa-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/

Both must fail with a certificate error. If either prints a page, your system still trusts the compromised CAs.

OS updates

  • macOS: installing all updates is not enough. Apple has not yet updated /etc/ssl/cert.pem, which /usr/bin/curl, git and elan use. The macOS section of the site Anne linked has the commands that remove the two affected roots. If you use Homebrew, also run brew upgrade ca-certificates.
  • Linux (and WSL): update the ca-certificates package. On Debian/Ubuntu, run sudo apt update && sudo apt install --only-upgrade ca-certificates. On Fedora, run sudo dnf upgrade --refresh ca-certificates. On Arch, run sudo pacman -Syu. RHEL, Rocky, Alma and Ubuntu 20.04 have no fixed package yet; the site Anne linked has manual steps for them. WSL distributions and containers have their own CA store, and Windows Update does not change it, so update each one separately.
  • Windows: update Git for Windows to v2.56.0(3), because it ships its own CA bundle: https://github.com/git-for-windows/git/releases/tag/v2.56.0.windows.3

Other tools

  • VS Code: update to 1.143.0 or later. Older releases trust the compromised CAs.
  • Python: pip older than 26.2.2 trusts the compromised CAs even after the OS fix. The exception is the pip from Debian/Ubuntu packages, which uses the system store. Upgrade steps: https://discuss.python.org/t/information-for-python-users-regarding-emudhra-emsign-ca-certificate-security-incident/109576
  • Node.js: Node uses its own CA list, not the system store. Update to 26.12.1, 24.22.1 or 22.23.4.
